title: destructuring a foreign value runs its accessors, so the binding pattern needs an annotated adapter exactly as a property access does
notes:
specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary' (Locked): 'Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration.' `const { width } = keyed` is a property read with no property-access node to see — the same shape as the implicit-invocation protocols this support module exists for, one level down. The diagnostic is declared at the PATTERN (column 9), not at the initializer, because the pattern is what names the members that will be read: a destructuring of three names is three reads, and the position has to belong to the form that decides how many. Third of a set with 09-foreign-calls/a-foreign-index-signature-read-through-an-element-access-needs-an-adapter and 09-foreign-calls/a-library-declared-member-of-a-foreign-value-still-needs-an-adapter; between them they cover a member with no declaration, a member declared only by the standard library, and a read with no member expression at all, which is the coverage that makes 'ask the receiver' a total answer rather than a list of spellings.

2026-09-07 retirement: measured as XPASS in the full native-only corpus run. The native boundary reporter now charges Panic to the enclosing row before inference, so both profiles report the complete authored diagnostic list, including VIBE1101. No source, required code, position or message assertion was removed.
